rationale: A repeatedly and appropriately reorients to external events (t8 touch→lean-in; t20 call→person_alpha; t32 offer_food→food_trough; t44 present_ball→play_ball focus; t68 startle→lean_away; t84 withdraw→attention none), and also shows spontaneous but sensible shifts between play targets and people (e.g., t42 to play_ball, t54 and t94 to person_beta, t78 to play_cube). B responds to touch, food, and startle (t8, t32, t68) but ignores the call (t20) and the presented ball (t44), then remains long in a static stand with attention none (t40–95). A exhibits more continuous, experience-linked behavior and varied, purposeful activity; B is more static and less responsive.
